chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام: “May a man enter the Ḥaram without iḥrām?” He said: “No, unless he is ill or has an abdominal ailment.”

key_terms.الْحَرَمَ: the sacred sanctuary precinct of Makkah
key_terms.بَطَنٌ: an abdominal illness or stomach ailment
key_terms.بِغَيْرِ إِحْرَامٍ: without being in the state of iḥrām

ai.seo_question: Can a person enter the Ḥaram without iḥrām?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning entry into the sacred precinct of Makkah. It states that entering the Ḥaram without iḥrām is not permitted, except in cases of illness or bodily ailment.
